subject: math

objective.text: Round numbers to any place to make good estimates in real world problems.

explanations.title: Smaller units are closer
explanations.text: Rounding to the largest unit gives the most zeros and the easiest number. Rounding to a smaller unit gives an estimate closer to the actual number.

explanations.title: Choose the best estimate
explanations.text: Look at the situation. Use patterns or data to decide which unit to round to.

explanations.title: Enough for everyone
explanations.text: If everyone needs one, it is better to have more than not enough. Sometimes you round up even if the digits say round down.

explanations.title: The largest unit can mislead
explanations.text: Rounding to the largest unit can give a number below or above the actual number. Choose the unit that fits the situation.

explanations.title: Multiply tens by tens
explanations.text: 3 tens times 4 tens is 12 hundreds, not 12 tens.

examples.title: Chairs for 2,837 students
examples.text: Nearest thousand: 3,000 chairs. Nearest hundred: 2,800 chairs. Choose by what is reasonable for the situation.

hints.text: Find the two ten thousands around the number. Compare with the halfway point.
Multiply the numbers. Then name the new unit.
Round both numbers to the same place. Then subtract.
Find the endpoints and the midpoint. Compare the number with the midpoint.
Think about whether each person needs one. Is it worse to have too few or too many?
Compare the rounded number with the actual number.
Think about what the number is used for. Decide which place makes sense.
Round each number first. Then do the operation with the rounded numbers.

misconceptions.label: Multiplies tens by tens and keeps tens
misconceptions.description: The child says 3 tens times 4 tens is 12 tens.
detection_signals: says 12 tens for 3 tens times 4 tens
misconceptions.response_text: Multiply the numbers: 3 times 4 is 12. A ten times a ten is a hundred. So the answer is 12 hundreds.

assets_required.why_this_method: The lesson uses a number line and a teacher's board. The child cannot draw it.
assets_required.description: A vertical number line with a lower endpoint, an upper endpoint and a midpoint. The child picks a place, enters a number and sees all five roundings side by side.
must_show_exactly: A vertical line with the lower endpoint at the bottom and the upper endpoint at the top
A midpoint mark with its value
A marker for the chosen number
A text box for a number up to 999,999
A choice of place: ten, hundred, thousand, ten thousand, hundred thousand
A table of the number rounded to every place
states_or_frames: Table of roundings to every place
assets_required.interaction: Child enters a number and picks a place. The line shows the endpoints and midpoint. A table shows the rounded number at every place.
assets_required.alt_text: A vertical number line with two endpoints, a midpoint, a marked number and a table of roundings.
assets_required.generation_caption: A clean vertical number line with labeled endpoints, midpoint and one marked point, with a small table beside it. [Build by code]
assets_required.review_notes: Source number lines are drawn by the teacher. Build from the printed values.

visual_generation_rules: Diffusion cannot count reliably. Any picture where an exact number of objects matters must be built by code (SVG or widget) or drawn by an artist.

Every visual must be checked by a person: the count shown must equal the stimulus in the question and the rubric answer key.
Animations are described as frames with exact counts per frame, so they can be built or generated and then checked frame by frame.
